title: Degree-filtration growth of a polynomial normalization
statement:
Let $F$ be any field [def-weil-field], $n\ge1$, $A=F[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and $Q=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$. Define $|0|_t=0$ and $|f/g|_t=\exp(\deg f-\deg g)$ for nonzero polynomials, where $\deg$ is total degree. Let $M$ be a nonzero commutative finite-dimensional reduced $Q$-algebra: reduced means that it has no nonzero nilpotent. For $z\in M$ its minimal polynomial is the monic polynomial of least degree annihilating $z$. If it is $Z^r+\sum_{i=1}^r a_iZ^{r-i}$, put $s_t(z)=\max_i |a_i|_t^{1/i}$. Let $B$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $M$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], and set $B(
u)=\{z\in B:s_t(z)\le\exp(
u)\}$ for $
u\in\mathbf N$. These are finite-dimensional $F$-linear spaces, and $$\dim_Q M=n!\lim_{
u	o\infty}
u^{-n}\dim_F B(
u).$$ The limit is along positive integers. No separability or assumption that $M$ is a field is required.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dim-algebra-artinian] to $M$ over $Q$, then [lem-sfb-reduced-artinian-residue-product] to its reduced underlying ring. Thus $M\cong\prod_{j\in I}L_j$, with $I$ finite and nonempty and each $L_j$ a field quotient of $M$. Give these quotients their induced $Q$-algebra structures. Each quotient is spanned by the images of a finite $Q$-basis of $M$, so $L_j/Q$ is finite; the structural map is injective because it is unital between fields. The ring isomorphism is $Q$-linear, since its coordinates are precisely the quotient maps. Write $B_j$ for the integral closure of $A$ in $L_j$.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 5.3.3/4, printed p.217, first paragraph; Stacks Tags 00J6 (lemma-finite-dimensional-algebra), 00J7 and 00JB (lemma-artinian-finite-length).

proof.text:
By [lem-trf-degree-valuation-orthogonal-basis], $|\cdot|_t$ is a well-defined multiplicative nonarchimedean real absolute value on $Q$, so the spectral-norm statements below apply over $(Q,|\cdot|_t)$. The product isomorphism carries $B$ onto $\prod_j B_j$. One inclusion follows by applying a coordinate map to a monic annihilating polynomial. Conversely, if each $z_j$ is annihilated by a monic $p_j\in A[Z]$, then the monic polynomial $\prod_jp_j$ annihilates the tuple, since in coordinate $j$ one factor is zero. By [lem-trf-product-minpoly-spectral-maximum], $s_t((z_j))=\max_j s_{t,j}(z_j)$: minimal polynomials are preserved by the $Q$-algebra isomorphism, since exactly the same polynomials annihilate corresponding elements. Consequently $B(
u)\cong\prod_jB_j(
u)$. The field spectral norms satisfy the ultrametric inequality and $F$-homogeneity by [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm], since every nonzero constant has total-degree norm $1$. Hence each $B_j(
u)$, and therefore $B(
u)$, is an $F$-linear subspace. It remains to prove the field case and sum its limits.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 5.3.3/4, printed p.217, product reduction.

proof.text:
Fix a field factor $L/Q$, put $r=[L:Q]$, let $D$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $L$, and write $D(
u)=\{z\in D:s(z)\le e^
u\}$. Choose a $Q$-basis $v_1,\ldots,v_r$. For each $v_i$, write a monic equation $v_i^{d_i}+\sum_{h=1}^{d_i}c_{ih}v_i^{d_i-h}=0$ over $Q$. Choose $0
e q_i\in A$ divisible by the denominators of all $c_{ih}$. Multiplying by $q_i^{d_i}$ gives a monic equation for $a_i=q_iv_i$ whose coefficients $q_i^h c_{ih}$ lie in $A$. Thus $a_i\in D$ by [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]; they still form a $Q$-basis. Choose $v_0\in\mathbf N$ such that $s(a_i)\le e^{v_0}$ for all $i$, possible because this is a finite family of real numbers.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 5.3.3/4, printed p.217, integral basis and constant before inequality (1); denominator-clearing written explicitly.

proof.text:
For $m\ge0$ let $V_m\subset A$ be the polynomials of total degree at most $m$, and let $N(m)$ be the number of monomials $X^\alpha$ with $|\alpha|\le m$. The polynomial definition [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] makes these monomials an $F$-basis of $V_m$. For $
u\ge v_0$, the $F$-linear map $V_{
u-v_0}^{\,r}	o L$, $(f_i)\mapsto\sum_i f_ia_i$, is injective by $Q$-linear independence of the $a_i$. Its image lies in $D$, since $D$ is an $A$-subalgebra, and [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm] gives $s(\sum_i f_ia_i)\le\max_i |f_i|_t s(a_i)\le e^{
u-v_0}e^{v_0}=e^
u$. Thus it lands in $D(
u)$ and gives the lower bound $rN(
u-v_0)\le\dim_F D(
u)$ once finiteness is established below.

source.place: Proof of Lemma 5.3.3/4, printed p.217, inequality (1).

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-field-integral-closure-finite] to the polynomial domain $A/F$, its fraction field $Q$, and $L/Q$. The finite-type hypothesis holds because the $n$ variables generate $A$ over $F$. It gives finite $A$-module generators $b_1,\ldots,b_h$ of $D$, without a separability assumption. By [lem-trf-degree-valuation-orthogonal-basis], choose an orthogonal $Q$-basis $u_1,\ldots,u_r$ of $L$. Write $b_\ell=\sum_i c_{i\ell}u_i$ and choose one nonzero polynomial $q\in A$ divisible by the denominators of the finitely many $c_{i\ell}$. Set $m_i=u_i/q$. Then $b_\ell=\sum_i(qc_{i\ell})m_i$, so $D\subseteq\sum_i A m_i$. This rescaled family is still orthogonal: for any $t_i\in Q$, scalar homogeneity gives $s(\sum_i t_im_i)=|q|_t^{-1}\max_i|t_i|_ts(u_i)=\max_i|t_i|_ts(m_i)$. Since all $s(m_i)>0$, choose $v_1\in\mathbf N$ with $e^{-v_1}\le\min_i s(m_i)$.

Proof of Lemma 5.3.3/4, printed p.218, monomial count and inequality (3); the shifted-binomial limit is written as a finite product.

proof.text:
Apply the field-case conclusion separately to every $L_j$ from step 1. Step 2 gives a finite product of finite-dimensional $F$-spaces, so $\dim_FB(
u)=\sum_j\dim_FB_j(
u)$ for every $
u\ge0$. Similarly $\dim_QM=\sum_j[L_j:Q]$. Taking the limit of this finite sum yields $$n!\lim_{
u	o\infty}
u^{-n}\dim_FB(
u)=\sum_j[L_j:Q]=\dim_QM.$$ All limits are along positive integers. None of the field-case arguments assumed separability, so this also proves the final clause.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N8-a07f27184 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read all eight steps of the item, both new nodes and every cited statement. The mathematics is correct and the item statement is unchanged; I repaired one citation. BGR itself is not in literature/ (the report marks it WANTED) and the network is blocked for this reviewer, so I could not compare against the source text. I checked the mathematics independently instead. Steps: 1 (finite-dim => Artinian, reduced Artinian => finite product of fields, index set nonempty because M is nonzero), 2 (B is the product of the B_j via the product of monic annihilators, s_t is the max of the coordinates via the product node, B(nu) is F-linear by the ultrametric inequality and |c|_t=1), 3 (denominator clearing), 4 (injective lower bound using Q-homogeneity), 5 (finite normalization tool use; rescaling the orthogonal basis by 1/q keeps it orthogonal, checked), 6 (degree bound deg f_i <= nu+v_1), 7 (stars and bars and the product limit, checked), 8 (finite sum). Small cases: M=Q gives 1, Q x Q gives 2, inseparable t^p=X gives p. lem-trf-degree-valuation-orthogonal-basis is stability of (F(X),|.|_t); it is true because the total-degree valuation is the discrete valuation of the hyperplane at infinity, whose local ring is Japanese. It is not a duplicate: the existing stability nodes are Gauss-valued, complete-base or transfer criteria. lem-trf-product-minpoly-spectral-maximum is true because the minimal polynomial is the lcm and the spectral value is the max of the root absolute values. It is not a duplicate of tate-root-spectral-formula or weak-spectral-completion-product. Both new nodes are statement only with five searches each. I accept the declared tool_use of the finite-type normalization node.
